flows.summary: Map a repo as flows -> steps -> code by agreement: list its entry points, hand briefs to independent passes, check their citations, and vote them into one map a human settles.

steps.name: Maintainer lists every entry point the repo exposes into inventory.json
steps.notes: Adapter is chosen per [[entry]] in flowmap.toml (here: cli). Other adapters (fastapi, rails, nextjs, pattern, list) sit behind the same adapters.entries dispatch; pattern and list adapters call back into lens.defs for symbol lines.

steps.name: Maintainer writes one brief per independent mapping pass (bottom-up or top-down)
steps.notes: Fills flowmap/RUN_SPEC.md with the repo's stack text (STACK per adapter), method text and flow vocabulary (or discovery mode when the vocabulary is empty).

steps.name: Agent running a pass checks that every cited anchor exists and every entry point is placed
steps.notes: Read-only; exits non-zero on any BAD citation or MISS entry point. Also run by the maintainer over all runs before reconciling. Anchor check is a regex for a definition keyword, not the call graph, so it accepts any same-named def/const in the file.

steps.name: Maintainer votes the passes into one map with evidence levels and a list of open questions
steps.notes: Flow vote per endpoint, step clustering by co-grouping (union-find), hop survives at >=2 runs; ties placed by handler-file affinity and listed in QUESTIONS.md.

steps.name: Maintainer names the proposed flows in flowmap.toml, pins split votes in decisions.json, and reconciles again
steps.notes: flowmap.toml and decisions.json are hand-edited (no command writes them); reconcile reads decisions.json endpoint_flow / confirmed_steps and strips `new:` from flows the human adopted into the vocabulary.

flows.summary: Trust and query the deterministic call graph: confirm every entry point's handler is a walkable node, and ask which entry points (and flows) can reach a symbol.

steps.name: Maintainer checks that every entry point's handler is a call-graph node
steps.notes: `callgraph check`; exits 1 when a handler's file is parsed but no node matches (adapter and builder spell it differently).

steps.name: Maintainer asks which entry points and flows can reach a given symbol
steps.notes: `callgraph impact <file:sym>`; needs map.json (endpoint_flows reads it), unlike `check`. Bare `callgraph` prints def/edge counts.

steps.name: Maintainer dumps the call graph as JSON at a git revision or the working tree
steps.notes: `callgraph dump [<ref>]`; borrows lens.graph_at for the revision read.

flows.summary: See the settled map: Mermaid diagrams at system/flow/step zoom, the interactive atlas, and the left-to-right canvas of screens, steps, code and data.

steps.name: Maintainer generates Mermaid diagrams of the map at system, flow and step zoom
Maintainer builds the interactive atlas page and browses flows, steps, merges and code
Maintainer draws the map as one left-to-right canvas, or redraws it from an existing atlas page
steps.notes: --from reads an atlas page's embedded DATA instead of rebuilding from map + code; --out overrides the path.

flows.summary: Before reading a diff, learn where a change lands: verdict (contained/spreads/blind), steps and flows touched, call-graph reach and reach diff, off-map code.

steps.name: Reviewer runs lens on base..head to get the verdict, touched steps, reach and blind spots
steps.notes: Read-only (markdown or --json to stdout). Builds the call graph and the entry-point inventory at both revisions from `git show`.

steps.name: After a git push or gh pr create in Claude Code, the PR hook runs lens on the open PR and hands the result to Claude
steps.notes: PostToolUse hook wired in .claude/settings.json. Runs once per head commit (atomic marker file), only when map.json exists; scrapes counts from lens's markdown by regex.

steps.name: Claude posts the pr-lens summary as the PR's single flow-lens comment, editing it on later pushes
steps.notes: `flowmap-pr-hook post <pr> <file>` is not a flowmap subcommand, so it has no inventory entry.

flows.summary: Turn a PR into a change page: chapters anchored to the map saying where it sits, what it changes, why, and what to ask, backed by facts and linkable from the PR body.

steps.name: Author pulls the change's deterministic facts as JSON to write the story from
steps.notes: `change <base> <head> --facts`. The story itself (docs/flowmap/changes/<name>.story.json) is hand/agent-written per the pr-lens skill; no command writes it.

steps.name: Author checks which story claims the facts don't back, each with the field and the fix
steps.notes: `--check`: JSON to stdout, exit 1 on any problem; writes nothing.

steps.name: Author renders the change page: story chapters (or automatic ones) over the map, with diff hunks last
Author gets a viewer link carrying the whole page in its fragment, sized to fit a PR body
steps.notes: `--link` refuses while the story has lint problems; past 60 KB it drops non-code diff text, then all diff text, then prints a drop-the-file instruction instead.

flows.summary: See a PR as paint on the familiar map: the atlas with PR overlays, or the canvas with a change and its story chapters numbered on the cards.

steps.name: Reviewer paints one or more PR ranges onto the atlas
Reviewer paints a change on the canvas, with its story chapters numbered on the cards they touch
steps.notes: `canvas --change <name>=<base>..<head>`; reads docs/flowmap/changes/<name>.story.json when present. Refuses --change together with --from.

flows.summary: Serve a static, no-network viewer so a change link renders in any browser without the page's data being published anywhere.

steps.name: Maintainer builds the empty hosted viewer page to deploy on a static host
steps.notes: Swaps the template's font block for a CSP forbidding all requests. Deployed copy lives in fjall/flowmap/; `viewer` in flowmap.toml (or FLOWMAP_VIEWER) points --link at it.

steps.name: Reader opens a change link (or drops a committed change page) and the viewer renders it inside the tab
steps.notes: Pure browser step: fragment is inflated client-side; nothing server-side runs.

observations: Three separate implementations of 'which symbols did this diff change': flowmap/lens.py:analyse (filters docstring/format-only edits via flowmap/lens.py:cosmetic), flowmap/change.py:facts (no cosmetic filter, adds new/deleted/modified status and class folding) and flowmap/atlas.py:overlay (no cosmetic filter, its own new-vs-changed split). change.facts then calls lens.analyse anyway just for the verdict, and flowmap/canvas.py:main calls lens.analyse again after atlas.overlay already walked the same diff, so a docstring-only edit can be 'changed' on the change page and canvas paint yet not count toward the lens verdict.

The same bounded breadth-first 'code under a step' walk exists twice: flowmap/diagrams.py:Diagrams.step and flowmap/atlas.py:step_code (same MAX_NODES/MAX_DEPTH, same noise skip), differing only in output shape.

State round-tripped through prose: reconcile records tie-broken split votes only in QUESTIONS.md (flowmap/reconcile.py:write_questions_md), and flowmap/atlas.py:split_votes regex-scrapes them back out of that markdown; flowmap/canvas.py:from_page likewise regex-scrapes JSON out of a rendered atlas HTML page; bin/flowmap-pr-hook:hook regex-scrapes counts from lens's markdown instead of using its --json mode.

Building the static, data-free viewer (flowmap/viewer.py:main -> flowmap/change.py:viewer_html) imports change.py, which imports lens, atlas, diagrams, graphs and config at module level (lens compiles CODE from config.app_dirs(), atlas/diagrams read config.load()), so `flowmap viewer` needs a git repo and flowmap config even though the page it writes holds no repo data.

flowmap/diagrams.py:Diagrams.write hard-codes text from the app this tool was extracted from ('workflow engine = `executor.run_workflow`') and tells the reader to override plumbing 'in decisions.json', while plumbing is actually read from flowmap.toml [flows].plumbing via flowmap/config.py:load.

Reads with side effects: flowmap/lens.py:defs calls flowmap/graphs/codegraph.py:outline, which runs a full codegraph index into a temp dir and fills a module-level cache keyed by file text; flowmap/lens.py:endpoint_set records failures into the module-global INVENTORY_ERRORS that flowmap/lens.py:blind_spots later reads, so blind spots depend on what earlier calls in the same process happened to inventory.

`flowmap callgraph` is three commands behind one entry point (check, impact, dump), and only impact needs map.json (flowmap/callgraph.py:endpoint_flows), so the reach check used during setup works before a map exists but impact does not.

Every command is dispatched by bin/flowmap via runpy after flowmap's bin/flowmap:project_python may re-exec under the target repo's .venv; the inventory's handlers (`file:__main__`) hide that dispatcher, so it appears on no step's code path.
